criteria.name: Report presentation
criteria.reasoning: Clear engineering structure with executive summary, contents, sections. Grammar generally ok. Figures present but not fully/correctly labelled with number/title/reference; tables lack numbers. Uses prohibited Wikipedia source and inconsistent citation style.

evidence.quote: outlines the intended designs and procedures involved in the construction of a Earth observation

technical_issues.issue: Uses Argument of Latitude as replacement for undefined true anomaly/argument of perigee; should use mean anomaly or state both undefined but still acceptable. RAAN described as launch site location 27.33° without proper LTAN derivation.
Claims max equatorial rotational benefit for SSO retrograde launch from Kourou; SSO launches actually benefit from near-polar site and require dogleg, equatorial advantage not applicable.
Relies on Wikipedia Timeline of spaceflight for launch manifests and NOAA blogs; prohibited low credibility source for engineering design justification.

overall: Solid coral reef SSO mission with STK analysis, clear single-sat rationale, Australian ground station and EOL plan. Minor orbital mechanics misinterpretations and referencing/formatting weaknesses prevent higher presentation mark.

feedback.summary: You delivered a solid coral reef monitoring SSO mission with clear rationale, single-sat justification, STK analysis and Australian-focused ground segment and EOL plan. Introduction and mission design are strong. Orbital mechanics descriptions and report presentation need attention to reach full Accomplished.
next_steps: In Orbit section, correct COE definitions: for circular SSO state e=0 so argument of perigee and true anomaly undefined - use mean anomaly, not Argument of Latitude; derive RAAN from LTAN rather than launch site latitude 27.33°.
In Launch, revise equatorial benefit claim: Vega-C/E from Kourou for retrograde SSO does not gain max rotational benefit and needs a dogleg; justify via polar performance and rideshare availability.

In Report presentation, add numbered titles and in-text references for all figures/tables, and replace Wikipedia Timeline and NOAA blogs with manufacturer user manuals, launch provider data and peer-reviewed sources using consistent citation style.
